verify.notes: V11428 Core claim holds. The slot is the node field of a static 0x18-byte VM handle {node +0, next +8, prev +0x10} in zero-fill (past the raw data of its section, offset 0xd33e90 on both builds). Its destructor 0x1441615c0 is registered with atexit (0x1449e071c) from the static initializer 0x1443a4a90 at 0x1443a4c7c; there is no constructor store. Teardown: if node != 0 it unlinks prev/next, clears next/prev (vmovups), fixes the node+0x28 head, calls Vm_Release_Node(g_Vm_Registry 0x146ca54f8, node) and stores 0 at 0x144161619, the only rip-relative write; +8 and +0x10 are referenced only in the teardown. KB rip-relative refs: 9485 = 8939 lea + 493 qword cmp (491 cmp reg,[slot] and 2 cmp [slot],0 at 0x14240c375 and 0x1442b9b87) + 52 loads + 1 store; 9083 in .xtls (14 of them outside .pdata) and 388 in .data1. Steam has the same count in every class. Signature: 1 hit in .xtls at 0x1406d20d8, lea r8,[rip+0x65cedb1] = 0x146ca0e90 (sigcheck OK). Steam: 1 hit in .tls$ at 0x1406d2118 -> 0x146ca2e90; the enclosing function and the teardown 0x144163b90 are identical after normalisation, store at 0x144163be9, atexit registration at 0x1443a724d. void * fits a reader of the value (a node pointer, NULL in practice). The 8939 lea consumers take the address as a handle pointer, though: Vm_Resolve_RegistryNode reads [r8] as the base node and returns the slot address on a miss. So the object is really a 24-byte handle. WRONG in notes: '477 cmp' should be 493 cmp; 8939+477+52 sums to 9468, not 9485. Not covered by the row: the 8-byte value 0x146ca0e90 also appears 12 times inside non-x86 data in .data1 (0x150b8ac68-0x151108e58, records that look like protector bytecode; neither exe has relocations), and 0x146ca2e90 appears 6 times in Steam .trace. So 'alike on both builds' holds for native rip-relative code only, and 'only store' covers direct native stores; writes through a passed handle pointer cannot be ruled out statically.

STILL WRONG: '8939 lea passing &handle (the whole handle) as a parent or base'. Most of them do not pass it anywhere. About 6788 of the 8939 are a null-object fallback, lea reg,[slot] then cmov reg,(obj+8) when obj is non-null (e.g. 0x1407a4af0, 0x141571f61: r15 = obj ? obj+8 : &slot, then mov rcx,[r15]), so the handle pointer is then read for its node. Only about 348 go straight into an argument register for a call (321 in r8, e.g. 0x1406d20d8 as Vm_Resolve_RegistryNode's base); the rest go through callee-saved registers or stack spills. Suggested wording: '8939 lea taking &handle as a default handle pointer, mostly as the cmov fallback for obj ? obj+8 : &handle before reading the node, some passed as the base handle (e.g. r8 of Vm_Resolve_RegistryNode at 0x1406d20d8)'. Minor: 'protector bytecode' for the .data1/.trace copies is a likely reading, not something shown (records of u32 fields with the address as an operand, not x86).
